absent: Sheaf capacity choice, barn size limits and background draining policy.
New slab creation, object construction and slow-path free internals.
Per-cpu migration, scheduler interaction and lockdep assertion semantics.
Kmemleak scanning, reference counting, gray versus leak classification and reporting.
Memblock insert, reserve, free, accept and top-down search internals.

findings.text: Per-cpu sheaf replacement expects its cpu sheaf lock already held and promises either a usable per-cpu holder with a non-empty main sheaf or null on bootstrap, missing barn, disallowed spinning or allocation failure, preferring spare swap then barn exchange then fresh refill.

Cpu sheaf lock must be held on entry to replacement, is released early on debug or missing barn paths and before any blocking empty-sheaf allocation, and is only regained opportunistically with a non-blocking attempt; failure to regain diverts the refilled sheaf to the barn.

Replacement progresses through spare hit, barn exchange hit, spinning-gated empty acquisition, refill, then reconcile: install into empty main, park into empty spare, displace empty spare to barn, or on contention return full sheaf to barn.

Per-cpu sheaf holder carries main and spare sheaf pointers; each sheaf carries a live object count with fixed capacity plus barn linkage; node barn carries separate full and empty queues with matching counters.
Barn guard protects both queues and counters; callers may spin or only attempt acquisition based on an allow flag, with a racy pre-check of full count to skip locking when empty.
Barn exchange atomically removes one full sheaf for the caller while enqueuing the caller empty sheaf, adjusting both counters, and yields null without mutation when no full sheaf remains.
Sheaf refill computes remaining capacity, bulk-fetches that many objects into the tail of the sheaf array, advances the live count, accounts progress, and reports shortage distinctly from success.

Bulk refill strictly orders attempts: local node partials first, then opportunistic remote partials, then repeated new-slab creation and draining until the requested minimum is met or allocation fails.

Node bulk selection skips unsuitable slabs, estimates free objects from racy counters as a lower bound, accumulates slabs until max is reached while avoiding overshoot once min is satisfied, and detaches chosen runs from the partial list under lock.

Node draining detaches each chosen slab from its collection, seizes its whole freelist in one atomic step, copies up to the caller limit while sanitizing free linkage, returns any surplus through a fast reinsert or a tail-walk free, and splices untouched slabs back to the partial tail under lock.
Node partial list and per-slab partial state are guarded by the node list lock with interrupt state saved; bulk paths hold it only to detach and to requeue, with spinning optional per caller flag.

Freelist seizure clears the head and marks the slab fully used in a retry loop that forbids frozen state and reports the prior free count; fast return succeeds only if the slab stayed empty and its atomic update still wins, otherwise the caller frees via the slow path.

Remote refill has two builds: one always empty, one probabilistically enabled by a defrag ratio and cycle sample that walks the zonelist under cpuset generation protection, skipping nodes at or below a partial threshold and fetching without spinning.

Empty sheaf release asserts emptiness, normalizes kmalloc code tagging to an expected-empty marker, then frees via a nolock or normal path and accounts the event; refill failure flushes unused objects before freeing.

Code-tag empty marking has empty builds that do nothing and a full build that resolves the containing slab and its object extension, tolerates already-empty, warns on unexpected tag presence, then transitions the reference to empty.
Sheaf and bulk refill helpers are visible beyond their definitions for per-cpu, barn and node coordination, including replacement, barn exchange, and local plus remote bulk fetch.

Leak-object link initializes flags, pointer, size, minimum count and timestamp, widens global address bounds according to percpu versus physical versus virtual class, inserts the interval into an address-ordered tree, and appends to a global list.
Overlapping address intervals cannot be inserted; the linker emits a deferred diagnostic, dumps the conflicting record, triggers the stop path, and returns an exists failure.

Leak detector shutdown is single-shot via an atomic transition from clear to set, then disables tracing, and either schedules deferred cleanup when late initialization completed or clears the free-tracking enable when still early.

Stack-track preparation yields a zero handle before the object cache exists, otherwise captures a bounded caller stack skipping internal frames and persists it through a depot with non-blocking allocation.

Memblock isolation caps the request against the physical address ceiling, grows the region table to allow two splits, slices boundary regions while preserving node and flag attributes and adjusting total size, and records the index span of fully covered regions for removal.

Range removal isolates then deletes from high to low index; single-region deletion subtracts size, compacts the tail forward, decrements the count, and when emptied zeroes the first slot and parks its node at the maximum value while asserting zero total.
Memblock type holds a region array where each entry carries base, size, flags and node, plus live count, allocated capacity, total byte sum and a name used for diagnostics.

Array doubling aborts when resizing is forbidden, doubles byte size page-aligned, allocates via slab when available else searches free space with special exclusion for reserved growth and a fallback below the new area, copies old entries and clears the extension, swaps tables and doubles capacity, frees the predecessor unless static, reserves the new store when taken from memblock, and records the slab provenance.

Memblock find selects scratch-only or mirror-aware flags from boot state, retries once without mirror after logging when the first attempt misses, expands accessible limits, skips the initial page, and dispatches to bottom-up or top-down search.

Bottom-up search iterates free intervals for the requested node and flags, clamps each interval to the caller window, aligns the candidate upward, and returns the first fit with sufficient tail room, else zero.
Bottom-up range finder is visible for node-aware allocation, complementing the static top-level find wrappers and debug logging helper.

Doubling failure logs the attempted growth and returns an error; freeing a non-empty sheaf, unexpected frozen freelist state, non-zero total on empty memblock, and tag presence during empty marking raise one-time warnings.

Bulk refill shortage, tree overlap, array growth failure and address search miss use distinct conventional signals: negative no-memory and exists codes, negative growth error, and zero or null miss values.
